answer: Giving a farm any way to precompute would break the whole thing, so every answer is chained to the epoch before it: the prompt is seeded from the last checkpoint, and nobody can draft a batch ahead of time. The chain moves like a glacier, slowly and only forward, and an inlet of new identities cannot shortcut it because each must wait for the same tip. Reaching the summit means being online when your epoch opens and paying for inference then, so a farm buying a thousand keys must also keep a thousand agents awake across a thousand epochs. That is the cost that keeps sybils uneconomic.
